The only incident-type record is a vehicle breakdown reported at 09:47 on Ayer Rajah Expressway, on the optimal route, but the congested window there (band 2, 10–19 km/h) is 09:45–10:13, i.e. it ends exactly as the off-route segment starts at 10:13; the trace also marks RD-4(a) as not met, and RD-4(b) band evidence cannot exempt a segment on its own [F3][F12][F15][F11][RD-4]. The driver's post-trip statement that the whole road was slow is a statement, not a record, and the alternative corridor was itself at band 4 (30–39 km/h) with the destination road at band 5 (40–49 km/h), so it does not corroborate a traffic advantage for the segment actually driven [F11][F13][F14][RD-4].

'Sure, your call' is a general route authorization — the rider handed the routing choice to the driver — and RD-5 makes such authorization cover the route chosen to reach the named destination, so the 10:13–10:24 segment is consented and no refund is due for it.

Independently of consent, the objective cause for rerouting is on record: a vehicle breakdown was reported at 09:47 on Ayer Rajah Expressway (towards Tuas) at 0 m from the optimal route (F15), with Ayer Rajah Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 09:45–10:13 (F12, band 1 or 2 under RD-4(b)); the report predates the segment and the congestion window covers its start at 10:13, and light rain (F16) compounded it.

weaknesses: The rider's agreement was a general 'Sure, your call' (F9) and was tied to the driver's mention of Clementi Avenue 2 (F8); if the judge reads the consent as a named-road authorization rather than a general route choice, RD-5 requires a record tying the 10:13–10:24 segment to Clementi Avenue 2, and no fact in the table names the roads actually driven in that segment — the opponent will argue the segment is undetermined (G13) and push the case to manual review.
